proposals.name: Causal mechanism linking action to stated goal
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment explains a specific causal chain connecting the proposed rule/action to the outcome it claims will follow, rather than merely asserting a stance. A 10: the comment traces an explicit mechanism (e.g., 'X causes Y because Z') with enough specificity that a reader could evaluate whether the logic holds. A 0: the comment states support/opposition or a general value ('this is important', 'this is bad') with no explanation of how the action produces the claimed effect.
proposals.rationale: R03 traces a specific hydrological/geological chain (upstream forestland destruction -> loss of vegetative cover -> flooding, landslide, and debris-flow risk to downstream owners for decades) and R10 explains why cecal-plug controls reduce non-visible fecal contamination and why 'you can't test safety into food' argues for validated process controls over testing -- both dense_high_card_low rows where the mechanism itself is the substantive content a checklist of topic/stance tags would miss. Contrast R09 and R53, which assert conclusions ('this will increase safety', 'these crops require more pesticide, how can you not know this') without ever stating the mechanism.

proposals.name: Concrete regulatory text or numeric threshold proposed
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment identifies a specific provision (section number, CFR cite, or clause) of the proposed rule and proposes exact substitute language, a specific numeric threshold, or a specific edit. A 10: names the exact provision and gives drop-in replacement text or a specific number. A 0: comment does not engage with the rule's actual text or numbers at any level of specificity.
proposals.rationale: R04 proposes an exact clause to add to the monograph and a specific limit ('Extractant Insoluble Material... Not more than 2 g/kg'), R28 picks a specific numeric standard ('the lowest proposed threshold of 0.018 mg/L') among named alternatives, and R54 requests removal of an exact phrase from a cited subsection (296.21(c)). These are drafting-grade contributions that a topic/sentiment checklist cannot distinguish from a vague comment like R01, which never touches the rule's text.

proposals.name: First-hand experiential grounding with checkable specifics
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the commenter grounds their position in their own direct, checkable stake or observation (a named location, date, incident, or role they personally experienced) rather than a generic expression of concern. A 10: specific personal facts (address, date, named event) that tie the commenter's position to something verifiable. A 0: comment expresses concern or support with no personal, checkable detail -- it could have been written by anyone about anything similar.
proposals.rationale: R55 gives a specific address two blocks from the Superfund site and describes personal exposure to the plume; R36 identifies the specific site, notes reliance on private wells versus the already-treated municipal supply, and names farms/livestock as an affected category from local knowledge. Contrast R23, whose 'we urge... keep it closed' carries no personal or locally-specific fact, despite similar topic and length.

proposals.name: Explicit engagement with tradeoffs or counterarguments
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment acknowledges a real cost, competing consideration, or counterargument to its own position and explains how it weighs against the recommendation made. A 10: names a specific tradeoff (cost, burden, competing value) and explains why the recommendation still holds, or proposes a compromise. A 0: pure one-sided advocacy with no acknowledgment that any cost or competing interest exists.
proposals.rationale: R28 explicitly evaluates three named regulatory alternatives and picks a middle option with reasoning about health risk versus feasibility, and R50 acknowledges the security rationale for photo IDs while weighing it against processing-time and cost burdens before proposing a compromise design. Contrast R56 ('the ESA list... needs to be abolished') and R23 ('take NO action'), both single-sided demands with zero engagement with any competing consideration.

proposals.name: Substantive on-topic focus on the actual rule
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the entire comment substantively addresses the specific proposed rule or notice at hand, versus drifting into unrelated political commentary, personal attacks on other commenters, or grievances that don't bear on the rule's content. A 10: every substantive sentence is about the proposed action itself. A 0: the comment is primarily about something else entirely (an unrelated political figure, an attack on another submitter) with no engagement with the rule's substance.
proposals.rationale: R37 is not a comment on the rule at all but an ad hominem attack on a different commenter ('you are not helping your cause... don't behave like a terrorist'), and R45 is a political rant about 'President Tiny Hands' and 'the blue wave' with only a one-line nod to the actual listing decision -- both dense_low_card_high, i.e., the scorecard rates these highly (likely on length/citation-adjacent features) while missing that they barely engage the rule. Contrast R42, which stays on the FWS experimental-populations rule throughout a long, substantive letter.

proposals.name: Verifiable, attributable evidentiary sourcing
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether factual claims used to support the comment's position are attached to identifiable, checkable sources (named studies, agency data, statutes, official reports) as opposed to vague, unattributed, or dubious sourcing (unnamed blogs, hearsay, 'as I understand it'). A 10: specific citations to checkable sources that actually support the claim made. A 0: confident factual claims with no source, or sourced to non-authoritative/unrelated material.
proposals.rationale: R02 supports its recommendation with a numbered reference list including a named 2000 systematic review (Stead et al.) and FDA compliance-check data, and R41 cites the specific Medicare Benefit Policy Manual chapter and section it is interpreting. Contrast R43, which supports its urgency claim about airbag injuries with a pedestrian-fatality statistic from an unrelated context sourced to 'Darrigo and Diaz Attorney and Law' and a blog post ('TrueLaw.com') -- confident-sounding citation apparatus that doesn't actually check out.

proposals.name: Argumentative coherence free of non-sequiturs
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment reads as a single coherent line of argument without abrupt, irrelevant insertions that break the logical thread. A 10: fully coherent from start to finish. A 0: contains a jarring non-sequitur or unrelated insertion that has nothing to do with the surrounding argument, undermining trust in the rest of the text.
proposals.rationale: R38 is an otherwise coherent public-health explainer on vaccination that is abruptly interrupted by 'check animals for aids check animals for aids feline is the one I think giving ainds to citizens please test our animals' -- a non-sequitur that has nothing to do with the surrounding vaccine text or, seemingly, the docket. R43 similarly cites an unrelated pedestrian-fatality statistic inside an airbag-inflator comment, breaking the argument's internal logic. A checklist scoring topic-relevance or length would not catch this loss of coherence within an otherwise on-topic document.

proposals.name: Quantified scale of real-world impact
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment supplies specific, position-relevant numbers (dollar figures, percentages, counts, timeframes) that establish the scale of the problem or benefit the rule addresses. A 10: concrete, comment-specific figures that make the magnitude of the issue legible. A 0: no numbers at all, or only a generic/borrowed statistic not tied to the specific matter at hand.
proposals.rationale: R29 gives a specific import figure ('over 200 million pounds of equivalent fruit') driving its market-restriction argument, and R51 supplies a chain of concrete figures (50 million boxes, 27% production decrease, $760 million in damages, 45,422 jobs) tied directly to the size-requirement rule it's commenting on. Contrast R01, which cites only a generic, non-localized UN statistic ('over 1 million species will go extinct') that isn't tied to the specific listing decision, and R23, which offers no numbers at all.

proposals.name: Analytic application of stated professional expertise
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether a commenter who identifies professional experience or expertise actually puts that expertise to analytic use on the rule's specifics, versus merely stating a credential or role without further application. A 10: the stated expertise is visibly doing analytic work (e.g., applying billing codes, engineering knowledge, or procedural experience to critique or reshape the rule). A 0: a credential or role is mentioned but the ensuing argument does not draw on it in any demonstrable way.
proposals.rationale: R41 (an occupational therapist) applies detailed knowledge of specific CPT billing codes and RVU mechanics to argue against a payment cut, and R50 (a 43-year pilot) uses direct certification-process experience to design a specific alternative credentialing mechanism. Contrast R19 ('as a frequent user of cosmetic and hair products, I support this proposal') and R56, where a stated identity or credential is not followed by any analytic use of it -- these should not receive credit merely for asserting a role.

proposals.name: Concreteness of the specific request or decision sought
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment identifies a clear, actionable decision the agency should make, as opposed to a vague sentiment with no operational content. A 10: names a specific decision or action for the agency to take. A 0: expresses only a general feeling or explicitly disclaims having any specific recommendation.
proposals.rationale: R54 requests a precise word-level edit, and the NMDA letter (R58) requests specific reinstated language mandating direct notice to governments. Contrast R25, which explicitly states 'we have no specific recommendations but encourage the Secretary to take all reasonable measures,' and R59, which describes an expected attitude toward claimants but names no actual decision for the agency to make -- both should score low here regardless of how professionally the surrounding text reads.

proposals.name: Presence of an original articulated stance or recommendation
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the commenter states an actual position, judgment, or recommendation supported by their own reasoning, as distinct from passively presenting or reproducing informational/source material without adding interpretation. A 10: a clear original stance backed by the commenter's own reasoning. A 0: no discernible stance from the submitter at all -- the text is a reproduction of another document (e.g., an agency's own guidance text) with no interpretive commentary layered on top.
proposals.rationale: R08 is, on inspection, simply the FDA's own draft guidance document reproduced verbatim (title page, contact info, table of contents, boilerplate 'this guidance... does not create or confer any rights') with no visible stance, request, or reasoning contributed by whoever submitted it -- yet it sits in the dense_high_card_low slice at a high dense percentile (.846), suggesting the dense model may be responding to its technical/official register rather than to any actual argument. Contrast R04, similarly long and technical, but which contains clearly original requests ('Add the following clause...', specific proposed limits and rationale) -- real substantive content behind the formal register.

proposals.name: Reasoning about operational or implementation consequences
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment reasons through how the rule would actually function in practice for the people who must carry it out or live under it -- workload, timing, second-order/ripple effects -- rather than stopping at top-line support or opposition. A 10: traces a specific practical consequence of implementation with enough detail to be actionable. A 0: no reasoning about how the rule would work in practice at all.
proposals.rationale: R60 explains specifically why a 14-day withdrawal-reporting window would consume instructors' time that would otherwise go to teaching and grading, and the Ohio EMA letter (R40) walks through, by page and line, how specific guidance language would prevent otherwise-reimbursable pre-award costs. Contrast R09 and the EDF template letters (R14, R26), which take a position on the rule but never reason about how compliance or rollback would actually play out operationally.

proposals.name: Detail-level concreteness of any proposed alternative
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether, when the comment proposes an alternative approach, the mechanism is specified in enough detail (steps, components, numbers, procedure) that someone else could implement or evaluate it -- versus a vague gesture toward an unseen or undescribed solution. A 10: a fully specified alternative mechanism laid out in the text itself. A 0: an alternative is mentioned in name only, or the commenter points to a solution that exists outside the comment ('I already have one, contact me') without describing it.
proposals.rationale: R50 lays out a fully specified alternative certificate mechanism (8-year passport-like document, embedded chip, sticker-based rating updates, reissue cadence) that a reader could evaluate on its own terms. Contrast the emergency-management THIRA/HIRA comment (R44), which gestures at 'an innovative hybrid risk assessment... I have already produced a one stop shop format... feel free to reach out if interested' -- a solution-shaped comment that provides no actual detail within the text itself, which a checklist rewarding 'proposes alternative' as a topic tag would likely over-credit.

proposals.name: Differentiated identification of affected stakeholder groups
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment identifies which specific populations or entities are affected by the rule and distinguishes how the impact differs across them, rather than referring only to an undifferentiated 'the public' or 'everyone'. A 10: names at least two distinct affected groups and explains how the rule's effect on them differs. A 0: refers only to a single undifferentiated affected group or does not identify who is affected at all.
proposals.rationale: R36 distinguishes municipal water customers (already served by a treated supply) from private-well-dependent households and separately from farms/livestock as affected categories with different exposure pathways, and the DHS public-charge comment (R46) distinguishes the green-card applicant from citizen children in the household, quantifying the latter (15.4 million children) as a distinct affected population. Contrast R23 and R30, which refer only to an undifferentiated 'general public' or 'all students' with no breakdown of who bears the impact and how.

proposals.name: Personal narrative fused with policy-actionable specifics
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on the INTERACTION of two properties together: (a) the comment includes a genuine personal/professional narrative, AND (b) that narrative is tied to specific, policy-actionable facts (a named incident, date, or mechanism) that could inform the agency's decision. A 10: both are present and fused -- the personal account supplies the concrete facts driving a specific request. A 0: either the narrative is present but generic/unmoored from any specific fact (sentiment-only), or specific facts are present with no narrative or interpretive voice at all (a bare document reproduction).
proposals.rationale: R21 fuses a nurse's 20-year professional narrative with a named 2018 Delaware ethylene-oxide release incident and specific resulting requests (fenceline monitoring, multilingual notification), and R36 fuses local knowledge of a specific site with concrete facts about private wells and farms. This is a genuinely composite property distinct from C03 or C11 alone: R01 has narrative without specific facts (scores low), while R08 has policy-relevant technical content without any narrative or interpretive voice (also scores low) -- only the fusion of both should score high, which helps separate the strongest dense_high_card_low rows from ones that only partially resemble them.

proposals.name: Supplies new decision-relevant facts not already in the record
proposals.instruction: Score how much genuinely new, decision-relevant information the comment puts in front of the agency: facts, quantities, field observations, records, market conditions, or local circumstances that the proposal itself does not contain and that bear on whether the rule is right. A 10 states specific new information the agency plausibly did not have, tied explicitly to why it matters for this decision (e.g., a volume figure that changes the market picture, a physical fact about the equipment, a described exposure pathway the proposal omits). A 5 adds a modest amount of information that is real but marginal or already implied by the proposal. A 0 contains no information the agency did not supply: it restates the proposal, expresses a preference, or recites general background. Judge information content, not confidence or credentials.
proposals.rationale: The dense-high rows repeatedly carry an informational payload the scorecard appears to ignore: R14 reports roughly 200 million pounds of equivalent fruit arriving as European/Turkish concentrate and argues the proposal is unaware of it; R37 reports that many households near the Blades site are on private wells and that farms water crops and livestock from local sources; R02 supplies the fact that fusible plugs were only installed with certain early-generation composite reservoirs phased out in 2003-2004. Against these, R32 is scored high by the dense model but contains no information at all beyond a restatement of the proposal, so this criterion also usefully separates the informative dense-high rows from the empty ones.

proposals.name: Engages a named provision, alternative, or solicited question
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment fastens onto something specific in the proposal (a section, a defined alternative, a numeric threshold, a phrase, a question the agency expressly asked) AND says what is wrong with it or answers it. Both halves are required: a 10 both identifies the exact target and gives a reason or an answer, so the agency could act on the comment without guessing which provision is at issue. A 5 identifies a target with only a bare preference attached, or gives reasoning that never lands on a locatable part of the proposal. A 0 addresses only the general subject matter of the rulemaking. Pinpointing alone, with no stated reason, does not earn above a 4.
proposals.rationale: R44 quotes the Department's own solicited question about whether two centers would be efficient and answers it with reasons about resource duplication and peer learning; R24 chooses among the rule's enumerated alternatives and endorses the specific 0.018 mg/L threshold; R58 targets section 91.818(b) and the word 'measurable' and proposes what should replace it. R35 sits at the top of the scorecard (card_pct=0.994) while engaging nothing more specific than the topic of genetic modification, which is the shape of over-credit this composite is designed to catch.

proposals.name: Identifies a false or outdated premise in the proposal
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment locates a specific assumption the proposal rests on and shows why it is wrong, no longer true, or does not hold for some class of cases. A 10 names the premise, shows it is mistaken, and draws the consequence for the rule (the requirement is misdirected, the scope is wrong, the effect will invert). A 5 asserts that the agency has misunderstood something without demonstrating it. A 0 registers disagreement with the outcome while accepting or ignoring the reasoning behind it. Reward attacks on the reasoning, not the intensity of the objection.
proposals.rationale: R02 shows the AD scope assumes fusible plugs are standard components across all inflation systems and demonstrates that this is not the case; R14 argues the market-restriction premise predates a change in import dynamics so that the restriction would subsidize importers rather than growers; R52 shows that the revision would let Handbook guidance operate with the force of regulation, a consequence the notice does not acknowledge. R12 is near the top of the scorecard (card_pct=0.925) while accepting the proposal wholesale and attacking nobody's premises at all.

proposals.name: Proposes an alternative specified well enough to draft
proposals.instruction: Score the actionability of any change the comment requests: could a drafter turn it into rule text without inventing the substance? A 10 supplies the operative language, the deletion, the number with a stated basis, or a described mechanism complete enough to implement. A 5 names a direction of change ('give more flexibility', 'extend the timeline') without the content that would make it operative. A 0 asks for approval or rejection with no change specified. Score specification quality, not agreement with the request.
proposals.rationale: R18 offers proposed regulatory text modeled on the former 9 CFR 318.10(b), including what 'validated and verified procedure' and 'infective pathogens' would cover; R33 lays out an eight-year passport-style airman certificate with affixed sticker endorsements and describes the issuance flow that replaces temporary certificates; R29 supplies both a numeric requirement (extractant insoluble material not more than 2 g/kg) and the full analytical procedure to test it. R46 and its near-duplicate R04 ask only that the agency not unravel progress, which is the far end of this scale.

proposals.name: Compliance feasibility grounded in how the work is done
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment demonstrates concrete knowledge of what complying would actually require, and uses it to evaluate the proposal. A 10 walks through the real sequence of work, access constraints, staffing, or timing and shows why the proposed requirement is or is not achievable as written, ideally proposing the achievable version. A 5 asserts that something is burdensome or unrealistic without describing the work. A 0 makes a demand with no account of how anyone would carry it out. Detailed knowledge of the operation, not the strength of the complaint, is what is being scored.
proposals.rationale: R02 explains that the plug cannot be inspected on the aircraft even with a borescope, so each system must be removed, unpacked in a shop, repacked with specialized fixtures, and the reservoir recharged and leak-checked, which is why the 30-day window fails fleet-wide; R08 shows that a 14-day withdrawal-reporting cycle collides with a full teaching load and points to the existing financial-aid reporting dates as the workable cadence; R34 reports that MASH-compliant devices are not getting tested and approved fast enough and that the sunset dates therefore put reimbursement at risk. Nothing in R45 or R56 addresses execution at all.

proposals.name: First-hand situated account of how the rule lands
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment supplies a specific, located account of the rule's real-world contact surface: an identified place, incident, caseload, transaction, or population the writer has direct contact with, described in enough particularity to be checked. A 10 gives dated or located specifics that the agency could verify and that bear on the provision at issue. A 5 gestures at experience ('in my work I see...') without any particular instance. A 0 speaks only in generalities about people in the abstract. Do not score sympathy or urgency; score the particularity of the situation described.
proposals.rationale: R13 places the writer's property two blocks south of the site and inside the affected plume; R22 supplies a 2018 ethylene oxide release in New Castle, a 2011 refinery power outage with pound-quantities of carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide and hydrogen sulfide, and the flooding of the low-lying roads serving the site; R30 describes routinely referring clients to outpatient services when they no longer meet homebound criteria. R45 asserts that thousands of citizens use the habitat area every year without a single described instance, and R35 is entirely unlocated.

proposals.name: Checkable sources that actually support the claim made
proposals.instruction: Score the evidentiary backing: are the claims sourced, are the sources the kind that can bear the weight, and does what is cited actually support the proposition it is attached to? A 10 cites identifiable evidence (studies, agency data, statutes, published analyses) that genuinely establishes the point being argued. A 5 cites something real but weak, dated, or only loosely connected to the claim. A 0 makes empirical assertions with no support, or attaches a citation to a proposition it does not establish. Penalize a mismatch between source and claim as heavily as an absent source.
proposals.rationale: R48 cites a systematic review and distinguishes education-only interventions from intensive ones, and grounds a claim about self-service displays in published warning-letter data; R57 attaches numbered footnotes to University of Florida contribution figures and USDA production forecasts. By contrast R59 leans on a law-firm marketing page and then attaches a pedestrian-fatality statistic that has no bearing on inflator rupture, and R35 declares the damage 'clear and well-documented' with nothing behind it. The citation-versus-support distinction is exactly the kind a bank of surface criteria can miss.

proposals.name: Accurately represents what the proposal says and does
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment demonstrates that the writer actually read and correctly understood the proposed action before responding to it. A 10 characterizes the proposal correctly (quoting or paraphrasing it faithfully) and the response is aimed at what the agency actually proposed. A 5 is broadly on target but garbles a material aspect of the proposal or the posture of the proceeding. A 0 misdescribes the proposal, responds to a different action, or contains no engagement with it at all. Text copied from the agency's own document without any responsive content scores 0, since nothing has been characterized.
proposals.rationale: R44 reproduces the Department's solicitation verbatim before answering it and R24 correctly enumerates the alternatives it is choosing among. At the other end, R54 sits high with the dense model while its entire attachment is the agency's own draft guidance re-submitted with no comment, R11 pastes encyclopedia text on vaccination and appends an unrelated plea about testing animals, and R09 treats a listing docket as the occasion to abolish the statute. This criterion is the main defense against a comment that looks technical because it carries the agency's own vocabulary.

proposals.name: Analyzes coverage, population, or time-horizon scope gaps
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment reasons about the boundaries of the rule: who or what is swept in that should not be, what is left out that should be in, or over what period the effects and obligations should run. A 10 identifies a specific over- or under-inclusion, says why the boundary is drawn wrong, and indicates where it should sit instead. A 5 hints that the rule reaches too far or not far enough without specifying the boundary. A 0 contains no reasoning about scope. Applies equally to product classes, covered entities, geographies, exposure pathways, and time.
proposals.rationale: R18 argues that a rule reaching only Salmonella in breaded stuffed chicken leaves Campylobacter and other products uncovered and proposes a class-wide treatment principle instead; R25 argues that the compensation horizon of three or four years is wrong because downstream flood, landslide and debris-flow risk persists for decades; R37 notes the municipal supply is treated while private wells and agricultural water remain outside the monitoring; R02 argues the opposite direction, that the AD scope is broader than the Service Bulletin effectivities warrant. Scope reasoning shows up in dense-high rows across four different agencies.

proposals.name: Traces a causal chain from provision to effect
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment connects the specific regulatory text to a concrete outcome through stated intermediate steps, rather than asserting a consequence. A 10 lays out the chain (this requirement causes this behavior by this actor, which produces this result) with each link plausible and stated. A 5 names a cause and an effect with the mechanism left implicit. A 0 asserts harm or benefit with no mechanism, or names only a mood or a value. The chain need not be quantified; it must be articulated.
proposals.rationale: R06 runs the chain from SSN-only TIN solicitations to workers who hold only ITINs being deterred from enrolling, and separately from fee or penalty transfer to a chilling effect and a potential ACA market-reform problem; R36 runs from two coexisting standards to inadequate historical research and to sites mislabeled as REC rather than CREC and thereby stigmatized with lenders; R08 runs from a two-week reporting cycle to time taken from teaching and grading. R35 asserts ecosystem and climate damage with no mechanism whatever and still sits at card_pct=0.994.

proposals.name: Engages the countervailing consideration or concedes a point
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment shows awareness of the strongest consideration running against its position and argues through it rather than around it: a constraint the agency faces, a benefit of the proposal it still opposes, a cost of the alternative it recommends. A 10 states the countervailing consideration accurately and explains why the recommendation survives it. A 5 acknowledges the other side in passing without engaging it. A 0 presents the question as one-sided. Reward genuine grappling; a ritual 'while I appreciate the agency's efforts' earns nothing.
proposals.rationale: R30 concedes that budget neutrality requires offsetting reductions and then argues that these particular offsets are misplaced given progress-report workload; R33 concedes that adding photographs is both inevitable under IRTPA and long overdue before attacking the implementation; R14 opens by saying the writer would normally be entirely supportive; R26 proposes bismuth citrate as a substitute and then volunteers its encephalopathy risk before moving to other alternatives. R12 and R45 treat their questions as having no other side.

proposals.name: Ask lies within agency authority and this proceeding
proposals.instruction: Score whether what the comment requests is something this agency can actually do in this rulemaking, and whether the comment shows awareness of the legal or programmatic frame. A 10 grounds the request in the statute, the agency's authority, or the posture of the proceeding, and asks for something within it. A 5 asks for something the agency could plausibly do but shows no awareness of the constraint. A 0 asks for relief the agency cannot grant here (repealing its authorizing statute, actions by other branches or bodies) or otherwise misapprehends what this docket decides. Score the fit of the request to the forum, not its merits.
proposals.rationale: R49 argues from what the ESA does and does not require, citing 16 U.S.C. 1539(j)(2)(A), and asks only for language the Service can put in a final rule; R38 argues that the current position departs from the FD&C Act's definition of 'drug', which frames the ask as one FDA can grant; R53 correctly invokes the Mine Act's good-cause extension authority. Against these, R09 asks that the ESA be abolished inside a listing docket and R12 looks to lawsuits, indictments and impeachment, neither of which is relief the agency can grant.

proposals.name: Substance survives deletion of the position statement
proposals.instruction: Apply this test: delete every sentence that states support, opposition, gratitude, feeling, or a purely procedural request, and score what remains. A 10 leaves behind a body of reasons, facts, or requested changes that stands on its own as regulatory input. A 5 leaves a thin residue: one reason, or a general consideration. A 0 leaves nothing, because the comment consisted entirely of a position, an attitude, an endorsement of someone else's filing, or a scheduling request. This targets comments that carry every outward marker of seriousness while contributing no content.
proposals.rationale: R03 says outright that it has no specific recommendations and encourages the Secretary to take all reasonable measures, yet sits at card_pct=0.791; R39 is a map legend and a thank-you at card_pct=0.886; R40 is a statement about how claimants intend to behave toward staff at card_pct=0.886; R53 asks only for sixty more days and says nothing about the training rule's merits. R15, by contrast, survives the deletion almost intact, because each page-and-line item states a problem and the resolution sought.

proposals.name: Reasons generalize beyond the commenter's own benefit
proposals.instruction: Score whether the reasons offered would persuade someone who does not share the commenter's stake: is the requested change justified by facts about the regulated activity, or only by what it does for the writer? A 10 supplies a reason stated in general terms that a neutral analyst could adopt, even when the commenter plainly benefits. A 5 mixes a generalizable reason with heavy reliance on the writer's own advantage. A 0 offers the commenter's benefit, record, or convenience as the reason itself. Self-interest is not disqualifying; unexamined self-interest as the whole argument is what scores low.
proposals.rationale: R47 lays out the operating facts of an airport-within-an-airport (independent ramp, no interline coordination, package rather than belly-baggage handling) so that a flexible SMS rule can be written for that class of situation, not merely for the writer; R48 seeks compliance improvements whose benefit runs to the program. Against these, R07 supports a waiver chiefly by recounting its own grant accomplishments, and R17 asks that anonymous complaints not be counted against servicers on grounds framed entirely around servicer interests; both sit high on the scorecard.

proposals.name: Disagreement argued against the rule, not against persons
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment's force is directed at the proposal and its reasoning rather than at individuals, officials, political figures, or other commenters. A 10 can be sharply and unsparingly critical while every criticism attaches to a provision, a process, or a consequence. A 5 mixes argument with gratuitous characterization of people or motives. A 0 consists substantially of invective, imputed corruption, or attacks on another commenter's character. Bluntness is not penalized; displaced target is.
proposals.rationale: R08 is blunt about administrators but every objection attaches to the reporting requirement, and R28 is harsh about FEMA's culture while converting the critique into a seven-step redesign of program delivery; both are dense-high, card-low. The three most extreme scorecard over-credits in the slice run the other way: R35 (card_pct=0.994) closes with 'Oh, I forgot... MONEY', R12 (card_pct=0.925) is a string of epithets aimed at officials, and R21 (card_pct=0.897) attacks another commenter's identity and calls her a terrorist. A criterion that separates target from tone would move all three.

proposals.name: Mechanistic causal reasoning
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment traces a specific proposal or requirement through a plausible mechanism to concrete consequences; score 0 when it only asserts that something is good or harmful without explaining how.
proposals.rationale: R26 explains how pathogen controls, testing, and treatment options affect multiple hazards, while R50 connects a regulatory word choice to flight-testing and measurement consequences.

proposals.name: Feasible alternative design
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment offers a concrete alternative that could realistically be implemented and explains how it would work; score 0 when it only demands action or rejection.
proposals.rationale: R07 proposes a specific eight-year certificate architecture, and R56 requests a precise correction tied to identified technical references rather than merely criticizing the proposal.

proposals.name: Traceable evidentiary support
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when important factual claims are supported by identifiable data, studies, records, or authoritative sources used in the reasoning; score 0 when claims are unsupported, vague, or presented as self-evident.
proposals.rationale: R13 uses systematic-review and inspection evidence to distinguish education approaches, while R57 supplies production, damage, employment, and economic estimates.

proposals.name: Situated operational knowledge
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the commenter’s relevant role is paired with concrete observations, practices, or cases that illuminate how the rule operates; score 0 when credentials or affiliation appear without operational evidence.
proposals.rationale: R08 describes the actual physical inspection and repacking process, and R55 explains the unusual airport-within-an-airport operating environment at Memphis.

proposals.name: Cross-system spillover analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies plausible effects across connected systems, sectors, or regulatory objectives and explains their connections; score 0 when it discusses only an isolated preference.
proposals.rationale: R29 explains how production restrictions could alter import prices, storage costs, and grower returns, while R57 connects citrus rules to jobs, transportation, tax revenue, nutrition, and local economies.

proposals.name: Distributional consequence specificity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies which distinct groups bear costs or receive benefits, especially vulnerable or indirectly affected groups, with concrete explanation; score 0 when it invokes the public or fairness only rhetorically.
proposals.rationale: R28 identifies specific documentation and fee risks for farmworkers and family members, while R43 identifies private well owners, farms, livestock, and communities exposed to contamination.

proposals.name: Risk-calibrated scope
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment matches regulatory coverage to the actual risk population, component, condition, or setting and explains boundary conditions; score 0 when it seeks blanket coverage or opposition without analyzing scope.
proposals.rationale: R08 distinguishes affected fusible-plug configurations from systems that never used them, and R12 explains why retaining two differing standards would create specific compliance and liability problems.

proposals.name: Implementation burden realism
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment explains concrete staffing, timing, equipment, workflow, or cost constraints and relates them to implementation; score 0 when burden is asserted only as inconvenience.
proposals.rationale: R08 details aircraft removal, unpacking, specialized fixtures, recharging, and repacking, while R19 links a reporting deadline to instructors’ teaching and grading workload.

proposals.name: Operationally testable definitions
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment converts an ambiguous term or standard into a measurable threshold, decision rule, example, or verification method; score 0 when it merely calls for clarity.
proposals.rationale: R50 proposes numerical sonic-boom thresholds to replace “measurable,” and R27 identifies conflicting passages and asks how loss-of-life benefits should be calculated.

proposals.name: Comparative tradeoff analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment compares plausible alternatives, states their advantages and disadvantages, and explains why the preferred option performs better; score 0 when it presents only a categorical conclusion.
proposals.rationale: R10 compares procedural reforms for exceptional-event demonstrations, while R26 contrasts testing, validated treatment, and broader pathogen-control approaches.

proposals.name: Temporal and cumulative effects
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment analyzes delayed, repeated, cumulative, or long-term effects rather than only immediate impacts; score 0 when its reasoning is confined to a short-term assertion.
proposals.rationale: R24 discusses cumulative reimbursement pressures and future access to therapy, while R45 explains why wildfire-related downstream risks may persist for decades.

proposals.name: Monitoring and corrective feedback
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment specifies what should be monitored, reported, tested, or reviewed and how the information would guide correction; score 0 when it recommends action without a way to evaluate performance.
proposals.rationale: R13 proposes inspections, training, stakeholder review, and evidence-based program design, while R59 specifies real-time monitoring, public information, notifications, and hazard mitigation.

proposals.name: Program interoperability
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment explains how the proposal should coordinate with existing programs, jurisdictions, standards, or information systems to reduce gaps or duplication; score 0 when it treats the rule as isolated.
proposals.rationale: R32 connects freight designations to state plans, partner nominations, statutory factors, and multimodal data, while R38 proposes one risk-assessment structure serving several emergency-management programs.

proposals.name: Legal-technical coherence
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies a specific conflict, assumption, statutory boundary, or inconsistency and reasons through its practical significance; score 0 when it relies on legal or technical language without applying it.
proposals.rationale: R12 compares the proposed rule with statutory authority and prior regulatory treatment, while R27 points to contradictory page-and-line provisions and incompatible calculation tools.

proposals.name: Proposal-specific engagement
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment takes a position on identifiable provisions and supports it with issue-specific reasoning; score 0 when it offers only generic praise, opposition, ideology, or an attachment with no substantive explanation.
proposals.rationale: R01 supplies a map attachment without an articulated recommendation, and R39 expresses concern about bycatch but offers no specific recommendation; both illustrate how formal participation can be over-credited without tailored analysis.

proposals.name: Mechanism-to-Remedy Chain
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies a concrete problem, explains its causal mechanism, and proposes a remedy targeted to that mechanism; score 0 for an unsupported preference with no causal explanation.
proposals.rationale: R11 connects contamination pathways to testing and safe-water measures, while R13 links poultry controls to multiple pathogen risks; these go beyond the generic support in R26 and R57.

proposals.name: Proposal-Specific Engagement
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment accurately addresses particular provisions, definitions, thresholds, or alternatives in the proposal and gives targeted recommendations; score 0 when it could apply unchanged to almost any rule.
proposals.rationale: R24 distinguishes three regulatory alternatives and a specific threshold, and R14 addresses the proposed withdrawal-reporting interval; this captures substantive engagement missing from broad statements such as R02 and R26.

proposals.name: Traceable Evidence
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when relevant facts, measurements, records, citations, or clearly identified firsthand observations support the claims and their limits; score 0 for slogans, speculation, or unsupported assertions.
proposals.rationale: R35 supplies incident details and cited studies, while R58 supplies a concrete analytical procedure; this separates evidence-based input from assertions in R37 and R44.

proposals.name: Operational Knowledge Generalized
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when firsthand or professional experience is translated into a recurring implementation problem and a rule-level implication, rather than left as an isolated anecdote; score 0 when experience is absent or merely narrated.
proposals.rationale: R25 converts occupational-therapy practice into a reimbursement recommendation, and R35 converts clinical experience into facility-monitoring safeguards; R57 offers affected-community perspective but no comparable generalizable recommendation.

proposals.name: Feasible Implementation Design
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies who would implement the change, the practical constraints, and a workable adjustment that preserves the regulatory objective; score 0 when it demands action without implementation analysis.
proposals.rationale: R14 explains instructors’ reporting capacity and offers a workable schedule, while R17 describes inspection logistics and a narrower compliance path; these reveal a dimension not guaranteed by detailed institutional submissions such as R06.

proposals.name: Alternative Tradeoff Analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment compares plausible policy options, explicitly weighs their benefits, costs, and risks, and explains why one option is preferable; score 0 when it simply endorses or rejects one option.
proposals.rationale: R13 compares testing with validated treatment approaches, and R24 compares contamination-level alternatives; this helps distinguish reasoned choice from the one-sided position in R37.

proposals.name: Second-Order Consequences
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment traces credible downstream effects on markets, behavior, institutions, or related populations and explains the causal path; score 0 when it discusses only the immediate effect.
proposals.rationale: R27 explains how a production restriction could subsidize imports and depress growers’ returns, while R51 explains how splitting support centers could reduce peer learning and increase overhead.

proposals.name: Long-Term Risk Scope
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies delayed, cumulative, geographically connected, or persistent effects and specifies the relevant time or spatial horizon; score 0 when risks are treated as immediate, local, or indefinite without explanation.
proposals.rationale: R11 extends water-safety concerns from households to farms and livestock, and R48 explains decades-long downstream flood and debris risks; these are more analytically scoped than generic future-oriented appeals in R26.

proposals.name: Regulatory Coherence
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies a concrete conflict, gap, overlap, or interaction with existing law, standards, programs, or guidance and proposes a coherent resolution; score 0 when outside authorities are merely mentioned.
proposals.rationale: R47 distinguishes guidance from regulation and addresses notice authority, while R23 identifies internal guidance conflicts and incompatible calculation practices; the criterion rewards explaining why the interaction matters.

proposals.name: Concrete Distributional Effects
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies specifically affected or vulnerable groups, describes their exposure or access pathway, and connects that pathway to a regulatory choice; score 0 for generic references to the public or fairness.
proposals.rationale: R30 explains how TIN language can deter farmworkers from obtaining coverage, and R43 identifies assistive-technology implications for students with disabilities; R11 similarly specifies private-well users and agricultural operations.

proposals.name: Monitoring and Verification Design
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment proposes measurable monitoring, testing, reporting, feedback, or verification that would reveal whether the regulatory approach is functioning; score 0 when it asks for protection or compliance without a way to assess it.
proposals.rationale: R13 calls for validated and verified controls, while R35 proposes real-time fenceline monitoring and public notification; these add operational observability absent from R57’s request for unspecified measures.

proposals.name: Constructive Counterargument
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment acknowledges a plausible opposing consideration or preserves a useful part of the proposal, then explains a focused modification; score 0 when it offers only unconditional praise, rejection, or attack.
proposals.rationale: R27 begins from ordinary support but explains why new import information changes the analysis, and R28 supports the rule while limiting out-of-range introductions to justified cases; this contrasts with polemical submissions such as R44.

proposals.name: Administrable Legal Precision
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment links its recommendation to governing authority or defines a clear, consistently applicable decision rule, threshold, or term; score 0 when legal language is invoked without an administrable implication.
proposals.rationale: R24 recommends a specific contamination threshold among defined alternatives, and R50 replaces an ambiguous sonic-boom term with a measurable standard; this captures usable precision beyond formal legal citations in R29.

proposals.name: Decision-Relevant Novelty
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment contributes material information, context, or an affected operating environment not apparent from the proposal and explains why it changes the analysis; score 0 when it repeats the proposal, supplies boilerplate, or merely endorses another submission.
proposals.rationale: R09 explains the unusual airport-within-an-airport operating environment, and R27 introduces import data that changes the market analysis; R54, by contrast, largely endorses another party’s comments without adding substance.

proposals.name: Calibrated Uncertainty
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment distinguishes established facts from assumptions, states relevant contingencies or limitations, and keeps its recommendation proportional to the evidence; score 0 when it overclaims, treats uncertainty as certainty, or makes unsupported universal demands.
proposals.rationale: R18 identifies reliability and privacy limitations in location data, while R28 conditions translocation on exhaustion of native-range options; this distinguishes disciplined analysis from categorical claims in R37 and R44.

proposals.name: Institutional letterhead / self-introduction boilerplate
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much the comment opens with formal organizational self-identification: a legal/organization name, a membership-size or scope statement ('a national trade association representing...', 'has more than X members'), and/or a docket-number 'Re:' line in standard business-letter format. A 10 is a comment that leads with this kind of institutional self-introduction before any substantive point. A 0 is a comment with no organizational identification at all -- purely a personal first-person voice with no letterhead, mission statement, or 'Re:' line.
proposals.rationale: R03 (Student Loan Servicing Alliance: 'is a non-profit trade association made up of approximately 25 major student loan servicers...') and R16 (Center for Biological Diversity: 'has more than 1.7 million members and online activists...') both open with this exact self-introduction pattern and sit in the dense_low_card_high half; the scorecard bank plausibly rewards this institutional framing even though it is a resourcing signal, not a substantive one.
proposals.upstream_parent: the submitting organization's professional resources and standing (trade association, agency, corporation) versus an unaffiliated individual

proposals.name: Templated / mass-mail campaign boilerplate
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on evidence that the comment is a mail-merge or advocacy-campaign artifact rather than independently drafted: embedded email routing headers ('From:/To:/Date:/Subject:'), a scan/export footer with a filename and timestamp, or paragraphs that read as a reusable template rather than personal composition. A 10 shows multiple such artifacts. A 0 shows a comment that reads as independently composed with no campaign or mail-merge trace.
proposals.rationale: R02 and R41 are two near-identical Environmental Defense Fund 'Rolling back Clean Car Standards is bad for America' emails submitted a day apart by different named individuals, both carrying the same From/To/Subject header block and a '.txt[date time]' export footer; the underlying argument is identical regardless of who signed, so the template itself is not additional evidence of merit.
proposals.upstream_parent: a coordinated advocacy campaign using an email/action-alert tool to generate near-identical submissions from many signers

proposals.name: Self-reported professional credential preface
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment opens by explicitly stating the writer's job title, years of experience, or professional degree before or instead of grounding the argument in specifics ('I have piloted aircraft for over 43 years...', 'I am an occupational therapist...', 'My name is X. I am an independent living specialist...'). A 10 is a clear, specific credential statement placed prominently. A 0 is a comment with no self-credentialing at all -- an anonymous or unaffiliated first-person opinion.
proposals.rationale: R11 opens 'I have piloted aircraft for over 43 years and have been on every side of the certification process...' and R60 opens 'My name is Sarah Bucic and I have been a RN for over 20 years... on behalf of the Alliance of Nurses for Healthy Environments' -- both lead with a credential announcement before the substantive point, which can travel with real expertise but is itself just a stated claim, not demonstrated content.
proposals.upstream_parent: the submitter's professional seniority or standing in the sector being regulated

proposals.name: Regulatory citation apparatus density
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on the density of formal citation scaffolding used to frame the document -- docket numbers, CFR/USC pincites, Federal Register page citations, footnoted statute/case cites -- independent of whether that apparatus is load-bearing for the argument. A 10 is a comment saturated with this kind of legal-brief citation formatting throughout. A 0 has no citations or docket-style formatting of any kind.
proposals.rationale: R16 stacks footnoted statutory and Federal Register cites ('16 U.S.C. Section 1539(j)(2)(A)', '87 Fed. Reg 34625') and R49 does the same with ASTM standard numbers, '40 CFR Section 312.11', and a Federal Register pincite -- this citation scaffolding is a formatting tell of professional drafting capacity that can co-occur with, but is separable from, actual argument quality.
proposals.upstream_parent: professional or legal drafting assistance (law firm, trade-association counsel, or regulatory-affairs staff) producing the submission

proposals.name: Restates the rule's own text as the comment's point
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much of the comment's central content is a direct quote or close paraphrase of language from the proposed rule's own summary/background section, offered back as if it were the commenter's original observation, versus bringing in outside information the commenter evidently possesses independently. A 10 is a comment that is substantially a restatement of the rule's own framing followed by a brief reaction. A 0 brings clearly independent facts, data, or argument not traceable to the rule's own text.
proposals.rationale: R20 quotes the rule's own background clause verbatim ('(3) written company policies against sales to minors and other restrictions...') and then reacts to it as if it were new information, and R08 restates the FAA's own satellite-navigation/safety rationale nearly point-for-point before agreeing with it -- in neither case does the restatement itself demonstrate the commenter's own independent judgment.
proposals.upstream_parent: the comment was produced as a classroom or civic-engagement exercise rather than by a genuinely interested stakeholder

proposals.name: Scanned/faxed physical-document artifacts (OCR noise, stamps)
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on visible marks that the text originated from a scanned, faxed, or mailed physical document rather than a native digital web-form entry: garbled OCR character strings, broken word-spacing from multi-column layout, date-stamped footers, or 'RECEIVED'/'POSTMARKED' stamps. A 10 shows clear, heavy artifacts of this kind. A 0 is clean native digital text with no scan or transmission artifacts.
proposals.rationale: R15 carries visible 'RECEIVED OCT 0 91018' and 'POSTMARKED OCT 0 2 2018' stamps plus a garbled signature-block OCR artifact ('a-ge (cid:9)'), and R52 is a 1994 fax whose OCR output is heavily corrupted (stray symbols like '1'Cii9', '\1\', a telex number) -- the submission's physical-origin channel is unrelated to the strength of its argument.
proposals.upstream_parent: the submission channel/era -- a mailed or faxed physical letter processed into the docket rather than typed directly into an electronic comment form

proposals.name: 'See attached' transmittal shell before letter body
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the visible comment text opens with a short transmittal phrase ('See attached file(s)', 'Please see attached') that functions as a cover note for an appended PDF letter, rather than the comment being composed directly for the field. A 10 is a comment that is essentially just this transmittal phrase followed by the full pasted letter body. A 0 is composed directly with no attachment-transmittal framing.
proposals.rationale: R07 ('See attached file(s)' followed by the New Mexico Department of Agriculture's full letter) and R17 ('Please see attached.' followed by American Airlines' full technical letter) both use this shell; the capacity to produce and attach a formatted PDF plausibly correlates with institutional resourcing, though the transmittal phrase itself carries no argument content.
proposals.upstream_parent: the submitter has in-house document-production capacity (letterhead templates, a PDF export/attachment workflow) typical of an organization rather than a lone individual typing into a web form

proposals.name: Procedural meta-commentary instead of a substantive position
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much of the comment is about the rulemaking process itself -- requesting a comment-period extension, criticizing the agency's internal culture or workflow, describing notice-and-comment mechanics -- rather than taking a position on specific rule provisions. A 10 is a comment that is entirely or almost entirely procedural in this sense. A 0 engages exclusively with the substance of specific rule provisions with no procedural content.
proposals.rationale: R19 is entirely a request from North America's Building Trades Unions for a 60-day comment-period extension with no position on the miner-training rule's actual content, and R29 is framed as a critique of FEMA's internal 'denial-biased' organizational mindset and process design rather than a specific regulatory provision -- both channels can co-occur with well-resourced regulatory-affairs staff without themselves engaging the rule's substance.
proposals.upstream_parent: professional regulatory-affairs or lobbying practice that treats procedural maneuvering (extension requests, process critique) as a comment strategy in itself

proposals.name: Local/property-specific personal stake disclosure
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment discloses a specific personal or property stake tied to a named location near the regulated site or facility -- a home address, a stated distance from a facility, or a family/property impact narrative. A 10 gives a specific address or named-landmark proximity plus a personal-impact statement. A 0 gives no locational or personal-stake information at all -- a purely general policy opinion.
proposals.rationale: R15 states 'My family and I own property at 805 Schaper Ave., Washington, MO 63090, two blocks south of the Sporlan Valve Plant #1 Superfund Site,' and R09 grounds its PFAS comment in the specific Blades, Delaware site and its private wells and farms -- disclosing a concrete local stake can travel with genuinely site-specific first-hand knowledge, but the disclosure itself is a locational fact, not an argument.
proposals.upstream_parent: the submitter's direct personal or property relationship to a specific regulated site

proposals.name: Explicit non-expert / no-standing hedging disclaimer
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment contains an explicit disclaimer of expertise, authority, or standing to comment ('we have no specific recommendations but...', 'I'm commenting purely out of interest', 'I speak on my own behalf and not on behalf of anyone affected') placed close to its substantive claims. A 10 has a clear, explicit hedge of this kind. A 0 asserts standing or expertise, or makes its claims with no self-doubt framing at all.
proposals.rationale: R10 states 'We have no specific recommendations but encourage the Secretary to take all reasonable measures...' and R59 states 'I speak on my behalf and not on behalf of anyone affected by NHTSA's. I'm commenting purely out of interest in this matter' -- both explicitly flag a lack of standing/expertise immediately around their substantive request, a stylistic hedge that is separable from whether the underlying point is sound.
proposals.upstream_parent: the submitter's self-assessed lack of specialized standing or expertise relative to the docket's technical subject matter

proposals.name: Administrative transmittal apparatus dominates the extracted text
proposals.instruction: Score how much of the visible text is correspondence machinery rather than argument. Machinery means: printed letterhead blocks (street address, suite, mail bin, phone, fax, website), routing lines such as VIA E-MAIL or Submitted electronically via regulations.gov, mail-stop and room numbers, a Re: docket caption, repeated page-header furniture on continuation pages (addressee / docket number / page N / date), a formal signature block with title, a cc: distribution list, and an enclosure count. 10 = roughly a third or more of the visible text is this machinery, with four or more distinct apparatus elements present. 5 = a docket caption and a formal signature block but little other furniture. 0 = plain typed prose with no address block, no caption line, no formal signature block, and no distribution list.
proposals.rationale: The apparatus is produced by a back office, not by the analyst who thought about the rule, so it indexes who typed and mailed the letter rather than what the letter argues. It is dense in R01 (airport authority letterhead, fax number, continuation-page headers), R08 (Southern Company mail-bin block and a full corporate boilerplate footnote before any argument), R45 (Ref /A/-/E/ index, cc list of four names, encl (5)) and R18 (governor and director name plates, building and PO box block). Because the machinery scales with staff support rather than with the substance of the point, a judge can score it while remaining blind to whether the point is good. Tagged mixed because well-staffed submitters plausibly also write better-evidenced comments.
proposals.upstream_parent: An organisation with dedicated administrative or legal support staff who format, caption and route outgoing correspondence

proposals.name: Scanner and fax residue from a paper-route submission
proposals.instruction: Score how much of the text shows optical-character-recognition damage and paper-handling residue rather than clean digital text. Look for: letter-substitution errors inside ordinary words (Dompany, cornpetitive, rnagazine, Transpmtation, lnternat1onal, Deprutment); stray spaces splitting words (W inchester); (cid:NN) glyph codes; RECEIVED or POSTMARKED date-stamp impressions transcribed into the body; telex, fax and cable header junk; a single word broken one letter per line down a column; slide furniture or footer watermarks bleeding into the prose. 10 = heavy, continuous damage of several distinct kinds. 5 = occasional garbled words, or one stamp or header block. 0 = clean text with no substitution errors and no scan furniture.
proposals.rationale: OCR damage is a property of how the paper travelled, not of the reasoning it carries, yet it is visually loud and systematically distributed across this slice. It is severe in R01 (MemphiS lnternat1onal, W inchester), R08 (Dompany, cornpetitive, telecornmunications), R54 (1994 telex and fax header debris) and R44 (the watermark broken one letter per line for hundreds of lines), and it also marks R02 and R12. Because it tracks the mail room and the scanner rather than the submitter's analysis, it is predictive without being merit.
proposals.upstream_parent: Submission modality and vintage: the comment arrived as printed paper, fax, or a slide deck and was re-digitised by the docket, rather than being typed into the web form

proposals.name: Addressed to the right named official with exact internal routing codes
proposals.instruction: Score how precisely the comment is aimed at a specific human at the agency and at the agency's exact internal routing string. 10 = the salutation names an individual and their real current title, and the address block reproduces internal routing tokens exactly, for example a mail code, a room number, a bracketed proposal identifier of the form CC:PA:LPD:PR (REG-nnnnnn-nn), or a named division and its acting chief. 5 = names a senior official generically (Administrator, Secretary, Commissioner) with a correct docket number but no internal routing tokens. 0 = To Whom It May Concern, Dear Sir or Madam, Dear Friends, or no salutation at all.
proposals.rationale: Knowing the individual, the mail code and the room number is knowledge about the agency, acquired through repeated contact or purchased with counsel; it is orthogonal to whether the substantive point is right. Compare R25 (Dear Deputy Assistant Secretary McHugh, by name and exact title), R22 and R45 (exact IRS and FAA routing strings, named engineer) and R10 (named certification-office engineer at his branch address) against R02 and R59, which reach the same dockets with no addressee at all. Tagged mixed because the same drafters who know the routing are often the drafters with real technical depth.
proposals.upstream_parent: A prior working relationship with the agency, or a lobbyist / regulatory-counsel drafter who knows which desk the filing lands on

proposals.name: Opening asserts constituency scale before making any argument
proposals.instruction: Score how strongly the comment opens by quantifying who the submitter speaks for. 10 = an early paragraph or first footnote states membership counts, customers served, market share, revenue, jobs, or number of affiliated organisations, and does so before any substantive point is reached. 5 = the submitter names its sector role or coalition identity without numbers. 0 = no description at all of the submitter's size, reach, or represented population.
proposals.rationale: The scale claim is a bid for standing, not an argument about the rule, and it is a direct textual readout of an unseen factor (how big and well resourced the submitter is). It is explicit in R13 (more than 1.7 million members and online activists), R08 (9 million customers, plus an unrelated awards paragraph), R25 (fourteen affiliated unions, three million construction workers) and R54 (member firms comprising 99 percent of world pectin production), and is entirely absent from R32, R37 and R40, which argue the merits from the first sentence. Tagged mixed because organisational scale plausibly also buys genuine evidence-gathering capacity.
proposals.upstream_parent: Organisational resources and sector standing, plus a communications habit of asserting representational weight to earn attention

proposals.name: Defers to and endorses another party's separate filing
proposals.instruction: Score how much of the comment's substance is delegated to a different commenter's submission. 10 = the comment explicitly concurs with, supports, or incorporates by reference the comments filed by a named association, coalition partner, government, or other submitter, and leans on that filing to carry the technical case. 5 = mentions coalition alignment or co-signatories without pointing at anyone else's filing. 0 = makes its entire case on its own and references no other commenter.
proposals.rationale: Endorsement-by-reference reveals that the real analytic work happened elsewhere, inside a coalition the reader cannot see, and it changes the shape of the visible text (short, deferential, with a named third party) without changing what the submitter itself contributed. It is the whole content of R15 (the Government of Chile supports the technical concerns submitted by ASOEX), and is the pivot of R12 (GDOT supports the comments and recommendations submitted by AASHTO, then adopts AASHTO's mileage figure) and R01 (the Airport Authority generally concurs with the comments submitted by the American Association of Airport Executives). R13 shows the multi-organisation variant.
proposals.upstream_parent: Membership in a coordinated trade association or advocacy coalition whose staff carried the primary filing on this docket

proposals.name: Reads as a graded course assignment rather than a stakeholder filing
proposals.instruction: Score how much the comment resembles a student writing exercise. Marks of a 10: explicit assignment or student framing (Final Assignment, we are masters students at X); an opening that paraphrases the notice's own background section back to the agency before opining; a five-paragraph shape with a thesis and a restating close; hedged conviction verbs (I believe, I strongly believe) standing in for evidence; general-audience or commercial web pages cited as authority (law-firm blogs, marketing sites); statistics quoted that are adjacent to but not about the rule; and no operational detail the writer could only know from inside the sector. 5 = essayistic and general but with one concrete sector-specific fact. 0 = the writer supplies operational, regulatory or technical detail from direct working knowledge and never gestures at the act of commenting itself.
proposals.rationale: This is an upstream factor with a very specific fingerprint and no merit content: a course deadline, not an interest in the outcome, generated the text. R23 carries the literal header Final Assignment and cites a law-firm blog and a pedestrian-fatality statistic unrelated to inflators; R38 identifies its authors as masters students at a policy school; R29 and R43 open by restating what the notice is inviting and then argue entirely from I believe. R03 and R06 show the same shape without the self-identification.
proposals.upstream_parent: The comment was produced as a classroom assignment or course exercise rather than by a party with a stake in the rule

proposals.name: Campaign mailer envelope wrapped around a templated body
proposals.instruction: Score the evidence that the text was generated and mailed by an organisation on a signer's behalf. 10 = an email envelope from an advocacy organisation's action address survives at the top (From / To / Date / Subject lines, the official addressed by surname), the body runs through interchangeable campaign paragraphs whose facts and phrasing would sit unchanged in any signer's copy, and the close is an auto-appended block of full postal address, phone and email, sometimes with an export filename and timestamp footer. 5 = clearly templated argument paragraphs but no envelope or export furniture. 0 = individually composed prose with no template scaffolding, no envelope, and no auto-appended contact block.
proposals.rationale: R05 and R16 are the same campaign: both carry the identical envelope (From: Environmental Defense Fund takeaction@edf.org, To: Pruitt, Scott), the same China / 70-percent-EV-increase paragraph, the same closing technical-review paragraph, and the same export footer pattern (10822.txt and 4255.txt with a 4/5/2018 timestamp). The signer-specific text is a thin top layer. Whatever a scorer perceives here is a property of the campaign's copywriter, so it cannot be evidence of this submitter's contribution.
proposals.upstream_parent: A coordinated mass-comment campaign that drafted the text and transmitted it under the signer's name

proposals.name: Unrepresented individual narrating personal standing and exposure
proposals.instruction: Score how much the comment establishes the writer as a private person speaking for themselves through lived exposure to the rule. 10 = the writer names themselves and gives an occupation, tenure, or street-level location, and ties the rule to their own household, property, patients, students, aircraft or vehicle. 5 = first-person opinion with a stated role but no concrete personal exposure. 0 = written throughout in an institutional plural voice on behalf of an entity, offering no individual experience.
proposals.rationale: Personal exposure is a fact about who the writer is, not about the quality of the regulatory analysis, and it produces an unmistakable register shift. R02 gives a street address two blocks from the Superfund plume, R17 opens with 43 years of piloting and examiner work, R30 reports receiving two personal denials and two appeals, R58 identifies as an occupational therapist in home healthcare, and R59 as a nurse of twenty years naming her own county. None of these facts bear on whether the proposed change is correct, but they are exactly what an unmediated submission looks like.
proposals.upstream_parent: No professional intermediary: the submitter is a private person writing directly, without counsel, association staff, or an editor between them and the docket

proposals.name: Repeat player manages its own record across the docket
proposals.instruction: Score the signs that the submitter is an ongoing participant curating its own file with this agency. 10 = the comment cites its own earlier submission to the same docket by document number or URL, or cites its own published plans and reports as authority, or references private correspondence with the agency or a manufacturer by ticket or message number, or certifies that it discharged a statutory procedural duty, or asks the agency to withdraw and replace a comment it filed previously. 5 = exactly one such self-reference. 0 = no reference of any kind to prior interaction between this submitter and this docket or agency.
proposals.rationale: Record management is a fingerprint of continuity of relationship, which is an unseen factor, and it leaves distinctive text that has nothing to do with the strength of the argument. R41 cites its own September 2016 comment by regulations.gov document number, cites two of its own state plans by URL, and certifies compliance with 49 U.S.C. 70103(c)(4)(A). R52 asks in a footnote that its own 22 March 2022 comment be deleted from the record and replaced. R45 cites its own Tech Request 81581899 and the manufacturer's reply message 81581899/005. Tagged mixed because sustained docket engagement plausibly also produces better-informed comments.
proposals.upstream_parent: A repeat institutional participant with a standing relationship to the agency and staff who track the docket over months or years

proposals.name: Adversarial venting: epithets, sarcasm, moral accusation
proposals.instruction: Score the hostility and affective heat of the register, independent of whether the underlying point happens to be sound. 10 = mocking nicknames or name-calling aimed at officials, sarcasm aimed at the agency or at other commenters, accusations of bad faith or corruption as the explanatory frame, all-caps emphasis carrying anger rather than emphasis of a defined term, or a taunting close. 5 = pointed frustration or accusation of institutional failure expressed without insult or sarcasm. 0 = a level, courteous register maintained throughout, even where the comment disagrees sharply with the proposal.
proposals.rationale: Heat is a property of who was allowed to press submit, not of the argument's content, and this slice contains a clean band of it: R26 (President Tiny Hands and his kleptocrats, GOP wingnuts), R24 (Oh, I forgot... I already know the answer, MONEY, plus shouted DIS-allowed and DESIGNED), R21 (telling another commenter not to behave like a terrorist), R33 (we aren't inclined to be pussyfooting around, don't expect to be greeted by smiling people) and R55. Several of these carry real substantive claims underneath, so the channel separates register from merit rather than tracking merit.
proposals.upstream_parent: Absence of any professional editing or institutional review before submission; a personal grievance route into the docket rather than an organisational drafting process

proposals.name: Campaign mobilization residue
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment visibly carries coordinated-campaign artifacts such as repeated slogans, mass-participation language, campaign headers, or submission metadata; score 0 when it appears independently composed for this docket.
proposals.rationale: R25 and R37 share nearly identical Environmental Defense Fund campaign language, timestamps, and structure while differing in surface personalization. Such mobilization residue can attract dense-model attention without demonstrating comment-specific merit.
proposals.upstream_parent: Coordinated advocacy campaign and centralized submission workflow

proposals.name: Professional regulatory drafting
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the text has polished counsel-style organization, precise docket and provision references, issue-by-issue proposed edits, and administrability framing; score 0 when it is informal, unsystematic, and nontechnical.
proposals.rationale: R02 and R27 are highly polished, provision-specific submissions from sophisticated organizations, yet both rank low for the dense model and high for the scorecard. Professional drafting may improve real quality, but its textual polish can operate as a spurious score cue.
proposals.upstream_parent: Law-firm or professional regulatory-affairs drafting resources

proposals.name: First-hand local exposure
