proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the commenter describes personal residence, occupation, direct exposure, or concrete local consequences tied to the proposal; score 0 when the comment contains no personal or geographically specific stake.
proposals.rationale: R38 identifies the writer's property inside a contamination plume, and R56 describes private wells, farms, and livestock in a named affected area. These fingerprints may drive dense scores through vividness and specificity, although firsthand experience can also constitute genuine evidence.
proposals.upstream_parent: Submitter's direct personal exposure or local victim status

proposals.name: Unpolished grassroots voice
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment has conspicuous spelling, grammar, repetition, colloquial phrasing, or novice explanations combined with an earnest personal stance; score 0 when it is professionally edited and technically standardized.
proposals.rationale: R01 and R13 use repetitive, unschooled prose with broad assertions, yet receive high dense percentiles. The dense model may interpret idiosyncratic authenticity as importance even though informality itself is not substantive merit.
proposals.upstream_parent: Limited editorial support and grassroots rather than institutional participation

proposals.name: Government letter template
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment visibly follows an agency or state-government template with official titles, letterhead-style blocks, enclosures, formal routing, and bureaucratic boilerplate; score 0 when none of those institutional-document markers appear.
proposals.rationale: R12, R46, and R50 are official state or emergency-management submissions with formal routing and institutional boilerplate, but all rank relatively low for the dense model. Government-document form can be mistaken for importance independently of the comment's actual reasoning.
proposals.upstream_parent: Government-to-government commenting channel and bureaucratic submission procedures

proposals.name: PDF and OCR production artifacts
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the extracted text contains page-number fragments, duplicated headers, broken words, scattered 'see attached' notices, OCR corruption, or layout debris; score 0 when the text is cleanly presented as ordinary prose.
proposals.rationale: R04 and R32 contain conspicuous pagination, repeated document headers, and extraction artifacts, while R20 is nearly only an attachment/map wrapper. These artifacts may serve as unintended document-level salience cues despite saying nothing about merit.
proposals.upstream_parent: Scanned-PDF, attachment, and docket document-production pipeline

proposals.name: Decorative citation authority
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when citations, statistics, URLs, or named authorities are numerous or prestigious-looking but weakly integrated, tangential, or used mainly to signal authority; score 0 when there are no citations or every citation is tightly connected to a specific claim.
proposals.rationale: R03 cites media and legal sources in a highly emotional submission without tightly integrating them into a regulatory analysis, while R58 begins with an encyclopedia-like citation block before an incoherent request. Citation presence may attract dense-model salience without proving merit.
proposals.upstream_parent: Copying, search-assisted advocacy, or authority-signaling drafting practices

proposals.name: Notice-language echo
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment repeatedly copies the proposal's wording, headings, or embedded questions and supplies generic agreement or disagreement; score 0 when it uses independent framing and develops facts not already cued by the notice.
proposals.rationale: R15 echoes the notice's wording about written company policies and training, and R24 reproduces the agency's supplementary-information question before rejecting it. Mirroring the prompt can look relevant to a dense reader without adding independent analysis.
proposals.upstream_parent: Drafting directly from the agency notice, questionnaire, or a response template

proposals.name: Maximalist scope expansion
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment uses the proposal as a springboard for sweeping ideological claims, multiple unrelated harms, abolition demands, or broad unbounded remedies; score 0 when it stays narrowly tied to one operational change.
proposals.rationale: R18 demands preservation of an entire habitat from all disruptive activity, and R45 calls for abolishing the ESA while addressing incarceration and private breeding. Broad agenda expansion may produce rhetorical salience and high dense scores without increasing rule-specific merit.
proposals.upstream_parent: Ideological or movement-based advocacy agenda

proposals.name: Institutional status display
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment foregrounds titles, membership or customer counts, organizational reach, prestige, longevity, or representation of many entities; score 0 when it gives no status or scale information beyond the specific issue.
proposals.rationale: R10 emphasizes Southern Company's customers, subsidiaries, history, and corporate profile, while R52 foregrounds the Center's 1.7 million members and national advocacy reach. Such status signals may affect perceived importance and dense scoring, although institutional capacity can also support genuinely stronger evidence.
proposals.upstream_parent: Submitter's sectoral standing, agency relationships, and organizational resources

proposals.name: Personal Stake Narrative
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment gives a sustained first-person account of direct exposure, loss, ownership, work, or personal risk tied to the rule; score 0 when it contains no personal stake and remains purely general.
proposals.rationale: R10 describes the writer's own denials and participation in input sessions, while R25 identifies the writer's own vehicle and personal safety concern. Such proximity may attract model attention through vividness even when it does not establish the proposal's broader substantive merits.
proposals.upstream_parent: submitter's direct exposure or affectedness

proposals.name: Credentialed Insider Self-Positioning
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the author prominently states a professional license, senior role, years of experience, or close occupational relationship to the regulated field; score 0 when no expertise or role is asserted.
proposals.rationale: R11 foregrounds 43 years across several aviation roles, and R29 foregrounds 20 years as a registered nurse. These credentials can be genuine evidence of relevant knowledge, but the textual status signal itself may be rewarded independently of the argument.
proposals.upstream_parent: submitter's sector standing or seniority

proposals.name: Coordinated Campaign Residue
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment contains recognizable repeated campaign language, mass-appeal slogans, campaign metadata, or standardized calls to action; score 0 when the prose is clearly bespoke and docket-specific.
proposals.rationale: R30 and R44 share nearly identical Clean Car Standards language, formatting, and campaign framing despite different apparent authors. The repeated rhetorical package signals mobilization and template exposure rather than independently developed substantive reasoning.
proposals.upstream_parent: coordinated advocacy campaign

proposals.name: OCR and Attachment Provenance
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the text shows document-wrapper language, duplicated covers, slide or page extraction, OCR corruption, attachment references, or other filing artifacts; score 0 when it is clean native prose without such artifacts.
proposals.rationale: R20 reproduces extensive FDA guidance text with attachment and page artifacts, R53 contains slide-extraction remnants such as vertically separated words, and R59 shows severe OCR and scan noise. These cues reveal submission provenance and resources, not comment quality.
proposals.upstream_parent: professional document production and docket-ingestion pipeline

proposals.name: Regulatory Redline Fluency
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment uses exact section, page, line, docket, defined-term, or replacement-language mechanics to propose a textual regulatory edit; score 0 when it makes only a broad preference without pinpointed regulatory language.
proposals.rationale: R15 and R31 carefully work through statutory and standards terminology, while R43 cross-references multiple aviation directives, bulletins, and figure changes. This fluency may identify a professionally prepared submission even when it does not prove that the requested change is meritorious.
proposals.upstream_parent: lawyer or specialist compliance-drafting support

proposals.name: Pseudo-Quantified Authority
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment accumulates precise statistics, dollar amounts, percentages, named reports, studies, media links, or numerical forecasts as rhetorical support; score 0 when it contains no quantified or attributed authority.
proposals.rationale: R25 combines injury counts, dates, vehicle years, and external quotations; R36 combines production forecasts, industry damages, tax contributions, jobs, and academic estimates. Numerical density can look evidentiary to a text model without ensuring that the figures are relevant, accurate, or dispositive.
proposals.upstream_parent: professional advocacy research and briefing support

proposals.name: Moral-Urgency Amplification
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the prose uses sweeping catastrophe, absolute demands, condemnation, intergenerational stakes, or highly charged moral language; score 0 when the tone is neutral, bounded, and technically dispassionate.
proposals.rationale: R27 frames the issue around protection for the greater good and future generations, while R47 invokes mass extinction, climate change, and demands a stronger listing. Emotional urgency may make comments unusually salient without adding rule-specific evidence.
proposals.upstream_parent: activist mobilization and issue salience

proposals.name: Enumerated Implementation Blueprint
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment supplies a numbered plan, multiple operational steps, process redesign, implementation mechanisms, or detailed alternative architecture; score 0 when it offers only a position or single requested change.
proposals.rationale: R02 proposes a multi-part pathogen-control framework, R10 presents a seven-step organizational redesign, and R38 describes a cross-program risk-assessment system. Structured solutionism may be an artifact of professional planning style rather than proof that the proposed design is sound.
proposals.upstream_parent: consultant, engineer, or managerial drafting culture

proposals.name: Institutional Prestige Wrapper
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the submission prominently displays government or corporate letterhead, senior officials, organizational mission language, or a high-status signatory; score 0 when it is an unattributed or ordinary individual submission.
proposals.rationale: R05 is submitted by an ambassador, R35 by a state agriculture secretary's department, and R56 by a senior vice president of a major company. Institutional presentation may cue authority and resources while remaining separate from the correctness of the requested policy.
proposals.upstream_parent: organizational resources and institutional status

proposals.name: Coalition Cross-Reference Density
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment repeatedly names partner organizations, prior submissions, stakeholder consultations, or adopts another group's recommendations; score 0 when the submission is wholly self-contained.
proposals.rationale: R05 explicitly supports comments from the Chilean Exporters Association, R24 endorses an airport-association submission, and R42 supports AASHTO while describing state stakeholder input. Coalition provenance can signal organized influence and information access, but coordination alone is not substantive merit.
proposals.upstream_parent: preexisting coalition relationships and coordinated drafting
